name: Corneal Endotheliitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Corneal Endotheliitis

criteria.description: Presence of corneal endothelial inflammation evidenced by keratic precipitates
Localized or diffuse corneal stromal edema associated with endothelial dysfunction
Mild to moderate anterior chamber reaction (cells and flare)
Evidence of viral infection (e.g., herpes simplex virus or cytomegalovirus) by PCR or clinical history

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of corneal endothelial inflammation with keratic precipitates and corneal edema, with or without anterior chamber inflammation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by laboratory testing for viral etiologies when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Fine to medium-sized deposits on the posterior corneal surface
searchTerms: white spots on corneal inner layer

pathognomonic.notes: Edema typically adjacent to areas of endothelial inflammation

common.notes: Due to corneal edema and endothelial dysfunction
Light sensitivity due to anterior segment inflammation

common.symptomName: Mild anterior chamber cells and flare
searchTerms: few inflammatory cells in eye chamber
small pus collection in eye chamber
mild hypopyon in front eye chamber

rare.notes: Blister-like lesions on the corneal surface
Due to chronic inflammation and trabecular meshwork damage
Resulting from chronic or recurrent inflammation

laboratory: PCR detection of herpes simplex virus (HSV) or cytomegalovirus (CMV) DNA in aqueous humor
Elevated intraocular inflammatory markers in aqueous humor
imaging: Specular microscopy showing decreased endothelial cell density
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating corneal edema
other: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing keratic precipitates and corneal edema
Tonometry showing elevated intraocular pressure in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly epithelial involvement with dendritic ulcers
Chronic progressive endothelial cell loss without acute inflammation
Presence of guttae on corneal endothelium
Bilateral involvement with gradual visual decline

redFlags: Rapidly worsening corneal edema with vision loss
Elevated intraocular pressure unresponsive to treatment
Signs of secondary glaucoma or corneal decompensation
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea: Fundamentals, Diagnosis and Management. 4th Edition. Elsevier; 2011.
Liesegang TJ. Herpes simplex virus epidemiology and ocular importance. Cornea. 2001;20(1):1-13.
Koizumi N, et al. Clinical features and treatment of corneal endotheliitis. Cornea. 2013;32 Suppl 1:S9-15.
